Local Design Lab · pass 2

Five candidates, in the real card family

Every candidate is built from idioms measured on the rendered Household, Children and What’s Next cards, and reviewed inside the real Focus Panel grid beside the real runtime cards. The question this page exists to answer is whether they look like one designer, one system, one product.

/dev/operational-card-lab1055px canvas · 507 / 1023 columns Avery Johnson · Johnson Familytypecheck rc=00 page errors

01 · What is reused, and what is new

The candidates reuse the real UniversalCard shell and the real body classes — household__{summary,row,row-name,row-detail,stats}, currentwork__{context-label,context-value,helpful-row,helpful-action,primary-action,recent-activity}, card-avatar, card-pill, card-detail--risk. Width comes from span: "row", which already exists in FocusPanelCardSpan and is already used by attention and primary_next_action.

Exactly one new primitive was added, and it is used twice: alloy-os-progression, a horizontal past → current → future band. Journey lays Business Process stages on it; Attendance lays the child’s day on it. Everything inside a column is existing vocabulary.

Journey timeline span:"row" · 1023 × 166

The spine is the configured Business Process stages; Work Views are operator lenses and are not history. One outcome line per stage, and progression is carried by connector colour rather than a banner. The current stage takes the Children --focused tint. At 166 px it is the shallowest card in the panel.

Open

No durable stage-history store exists, so past entry dates come from events and a skipped stage can only be inferred. A Milestones card is registered and permanently empty — the recommendation stands that Journey absorbs it rather than adding a second answer to one question.

Health & Safety status span:1 · 507 × 569

An information card, not an evaluation — no Complete / Needs attention / Severe taxonomy anywhere. The severe allergy is prominent because the fact itself is red, not because a count is announced. Missing required information is amber inside its own section, so enrollment-blocking gaps are visible without duplicating Readiness. Emergency contacts are Household’s truth, so the card shows the first call and a count chip.

Open

Child health facts have no canonical Alloy store today, and the category and severity vocabulary needs an owner. Whether medication authorization is an enrollment requirement or a health fact decides which section owns it.

Staff collection span:1 · 507 × 422

Deliberately the closest relative of Household and Children — same avatar, same name weight, same pill slot, same label-over-value pair. Why a person is relevant is carried by the pill plus the room line, never by category headings. Scope is the child’s site, program, room and today; the enrollment owner is one more row with its own pill and its own labels (Owns / This enrollment), never a second section.

Open

Which relationships appear should be configuration, and there is no staff-to-child relationship config surface yet. Staff room assignment is staff_presence truth while the child-to-room link is scheduling truth — one resolver has to join them.

Attendance timeline span:"row" · 1023 × 331

A pure projection of the existing ChildAttendanceReadModel — no second attendance model. Classroom movement is real truth: room_transfer is a first-class event kind carrying from_room_location_id / to_room_location_id. Nothing here is an editable field — corrections are entry_type: correction | reversal events, so every path is an action, in the What’s Next button row. The bar states expected window against actual-so-far; the band carries the events.

Open

Child attendance has no registered capability — staff has staff_presence.*, the child side has nothing — so these actions have no action key to call yet.

Billing status span:"row" · 1023 × 401

Three zones across one row, separated only by the grid gap. Payers are one line each — name, share, method — kept distinct from the household primary contact, and a funding source is a payer like any other. Emphasis follows state: Pay now is filled while anything is past due. Recent activity is a preview capped at five, matching Timeline’s SUMMARY_MAX rule. The card carries the family’s one permitted rule, above the family-share total, because the card is arithmetic.

Open

Alloy has a charge substrate but no family-grain posted balance, billing period, autopay or payment-method health. Subsidy and responsibility split have no canonical model — the payer rows are the shape a model would need to fill.

03 · Corrections made during the pass

Each was caught by putting a candidate next to a live card, not by reading the code.

  1. 1Section rules. I gave every section head a hairline. The family has exactly one, in What’s Next before RECENT ACTIVITY, where a different kind of content follows the action row. Removed — like content now separates with whitespace, as Household and Children do.
  2. 2The primary action. I invented a tinted outline. The family’s primary action is the filled bend-pine currentwork__primary-action. Replaced, so Check out and Pay now match Contact Family exactly.
  3. 3The Attendance track. Positional ticks implied an alignment with the equal-width event columns that does not exist. The bar now states only expected window against actual-so-far.
  4. 4Billing balance. Zone one was three times the height of the others. Payers became one line each — which is also the shape the brief asked for.
  5. 5Staff labels. Room / Today are wrong for an enrollment owner. Labels are per-person truth.
  6. 6Missing rendered grey because the base value colour won the cascade. Now amber.
  7. 7Mark absent is not a sensible action while a child is Present. Three actions, as What’s Next.

04 · Containment

No candidate appears in FOCUS_PANEL_CARD_KEYS, FOCUS_PANEL_CARDS, FOCUS_PANEL_CARD_CATALOG, SYSTEM5_CARD_ARCHETYPE or focusPanelCardProviders. Candidate CSS is lab-scoped, not in alloyOsRuntime.css. The only production file touched is a superseded banner on the rejected spec. No production module imports cardLab.

Four HTTP 400/404s appear in the lab. They come from the real runtime cards fetching for the demo subject demo-opp-1, which has no database row — the candidates make no network requests at all. Edge, empty and error states are written into the components but are deliberately not reviewed yet.
